scanMode: regression (c91bc1a..3a96fb7, story-003) - reasoning performed over the WHOLE of src/Antimatter.sol at 3a96fb7, not only the changed lines
inputsConsumed: lib/antimatter/lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol (read to establish the reachable end state of mintedForStable == 0)
coverageCaveat: Tier-1 SAST produced ZERO detector records on the new lines 256-266. Every finding below rests on manual reading plus the project's own test assertions, never on tool silence.

findings.severityArgument: Honest weighing. The loss it enables is real (the caller's entire stablecoin half, at whatever the live rate is) but it requires a second condition - an adverse rate move - to bite, and the NatSpec does state the combined-total semantics. Escalate to Medium only if the classifier accepts that a whole contiguous range of parameter values silently meaning `no protection` is a protocol-induced defect rather than caller error. See knownInvalidAdjacency.
findings.ledgerCorrespondence: GENUINELY NEW. No existing fingerprint covers it: the parameter it is about did not exist before 3a96fb7. Proposed fingerprintBasis `src/Antimatter.sol:annihilate:CombinedTotalFloorInertBelowAmount` (rootCauseClass CombinedTotalFloorInertBelowAmount). It is the RESIDUAL of the F-01 fix, not a re-file of F-01, and it must not be collapsed into 3aac91383dcb6060 - F-01 is `there is no minimum-output parameter`, which is now false.
findings.description: The only value check on the stablecoin half is `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` at :260, where `totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable` (:259). `mintedForStable` is a uint256 and is therefore >= 0, so `totalPhUSD >= amount` unconditionally (profile INV-8). The predicate at :260 is consequently UNSATISFIABLE for every `minPhUSDOut` in [0, amount] - not merely for zero. Passing 1 wei, or `amount`, or anything between, is byte-for-byte equivalent to passing 0. The protection actually purchased is exactly `minPhUSDOut - amount`, and it is zero or negative across the whole natural-unit range. The contract does nothing to reject, warn about, or record an inert floor: there is no `require(minPhUSDOut > amount)`, and `Annihilated` (:266) logs `totalPhUSD` but NOT `minPhUSDOut`, so an inert floor and an honoured floor are indistinguishable both on chain (the log) and off (the receipt).
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore;   // :256

// The caller's floor, measured against the total both halves come to.
uint256 totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable;                             // :259
if (totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut) revert InsufficientPhUSDOut(minPhUSDOut, totalPhUSD);  // :260

_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount);                                            // :263
IERC20(address(_phUSD)).safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable);          // :264

emit Annihilated(stable, msg.sender, recipient, amount, stableAmount, totalPhUSD);  // :266  <- minPhUSDOut not logged
findings.attackVector: No attacker is required; the reachable end state is reached by an honest caller. The natural quantity for a caller to think of as `the minimum I will accept` is what their STABLECOIN half must fetch - that is the only leg that can move, and it is the leg the parameter was added to protect (ledger F-01 fixPlan_2026_08_21). A caller annihilating 100e18 AM against 100e6 USDC who computes `my stable half must fetch at least 100 phUSD` and passes `minPhUSDOut = 100e18` lands EXACTLY on the inert boundary: `amount` is 100e18, so the guard cannot fire. If the minter's exchangeRate is then 0 (or anything at all - 6e17, 1e12, 0), the call settles, the 100e6 USDC is pulled and deposited into the yield strategy permanently, and the caller receives only the 100e18 antimatter half. The caller stated a floor, the transaction succeeded, and the floor bought nothing. Correct usage requires `minPhUSDOut = amount + expectedStableHalf` (i.e. 200e18), which the NatSpec at :222-225 does state but which inverts the intuitive unit.
findings.reachableEndState: Caller's stablecoin half irreversibly deposited into the yield strategy under the minter's custody; caller receives amount phUSD instead of the amount + expectedStableHalf they set a floor for; no revert, no distinguishing event field, no on-chain trace that a floor was ever stated.
findings.evidenceFromProjectsOwnSuite: test/Annihilation.t.sol:374 test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor ASSERTS this exact end state as intended for minPhUSDOut == 0 (rate set to 0; `assertEq(phUSD.balanceOf(user), 100 ether, "only the antimatter half")`, `assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(user), 0, "the stable half was still taken")`). The identical assertions would hold for any minPhUSDOut in [1, 100 ether] - and no test in the suite passes such a value.
findings.whyTheOldCodeDidNotHaveThis: At c91bc1a the stablecoin half was anchored by `if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(...)` and, pre-burn, by `if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();`. Both are deleted. Nothing protocol-side replaced them; the replacement is entirely caller-supplied and, over the natural-unit range, inert.
findings.documentationGap: NatSpec :224-225 sanctions `minPhUSDOut == 0` as an explicit waiver. It does not state that [1, amount] is an equally complete waiver. A reader of the parameter doc is told that zero is the opt-out, which implies non-zero is opt-in.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Either (a) reject an inert floor - `if (minPhUSDOut != 0 && minPhUSDOut <= amount) revert FloorBelowGuaranteedHalf(minPhUSDOut, amount);`, preserving the documented zero waiver while making every other inert value fail loudly; or (b) express the floor on the leg that can actually move - `minStableHalfOut`, checked as `mintedForStable < minStableHalfOut`, which has no inert range at all and matches the unit a caller naturally computes. Independently, add `minPhUSDOut` to the `Annihilated` event so an inert floor is at least observable after the fact.
findings.knownInvalidAdjacency: PARKED VISIBLY, NOT DROPPED. C4 lists `user input mistakes` as known-invalid, and a caller passing the wrong minOut is adjacent to that. The reason this is filed rather than suppressed: the defect is not that a caller can mistype a number, it is that a contiguous, natural-unit range of WELL-FORMED values is structurally a no-op with no diagnostic, because the guard is placed on a total half of which is a constant. That is a property of the contract's design, not of the caller's typing.
findings.law3: Not an owner finding. No owner action is required.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: RECONCILES TO EXISTING LEDGER ENTRY ad4b779566291190 (L-01, issueId am1l1, status open, severity qa). NO NEW FINGERPRINT IS MINTED. The root cause - `mintedForStable` is a balance delta with no provenance test - has never moved; only its impact has, twice.
findings.verdict: THE ORIGINAL run-01 IMPACT IS RESTORED. The ledger's fixPlan_2026_08_21 predicted this ('L-01 IMPACT RE-INVERTS'); the prediction is CONFIRMED against 3a96fb7 source.
findings.description: `mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore` (:256) attributes to the caller-chosen `recipient` every wei of phUSD that arrived on Antimatter in the window [:244, :256], regardless of who sent it, and forwards it verbatim at :264. At c91bc1a the deleted `PhUSDAmountMismatch` equality check was the ONLY thing that caught such an arrival, converting the leak into a revert (run-02's 'griefing brick' framing, on which the 2026-08-20 human QA downgrade was reasoned). That check is gone. The new floor at :260 cannot substitute for it in either direction: mid-call injection RAISES `mintedForStable`, so it raises `totalPhUSD`, so it passes any minimum-output check BY CONSTRUCTION. A one-sided floor is structurally incapable of catching an over-credit.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 phUSDBefore = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this));        // :244
...
minter.mint(stable, stableAmount);                            // :251  <- untrusted `stable` code runs inside this (the minter pulls it)
...
uint256 mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore;  // :256  no provenance test, no anchor
uint256 totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable;                // :259  injection RAISES this
if (totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut) revert ...;                     // :260  a floor can never catch an over-credit
IERC20(address(_phUSD)).safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable);         // :264  forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient
findings.attackVector: Cross-contract, via the one inbound-callback surface the profile identifies: an owner-registered `stable` with a transfer hook. Its hook runs during the pull at :246 and again when the minter pulls at :251, both inside the window. Any phUSD it (or the yield strategy, or any third party it calls) moves to Antimatter in that window is swept to `recipient`. Run-01's PoC (workspace/antimatter/test/audit/Tier2b.t.sol::test_midCallPhUSDInjectionIsForwardedToRecipient) demonstrated exactly this: 500e18 injected from the stable's hook, annihilator received 700e18. That PoC targets the pre-c91bc1a code shape, which 3a96fb7 has restored on this line. The control test in the same file confirms a PRE-call donation is correctly excluded by the :244 snapshot, so the window is genuinely [:244,:256] and not wider.
findings.reachableEndState: phUSD belonging to no one in this transaction leaves Antimatter to an address the caller nominated. Antimatter's own phUSD balance still nets to zero, so INV-6 and the suite's `phUSD.balanceOf(address(antimatter)) == 0` assertions (test/Annihilation.t.sol:326, :341) remain green throughout - the leak is invisible to every existing assertion.
findings.subDefectStillPresent: The mirror case is unchanged: if Antimatter's phUSD balance DECREASES inside the window, :256 reverts with a bare Panic(0x11) rather than a named error.
findings.severityRecommendation: RE-EXAMINE, DO NOT CARRY OVER UNREAD. The 2026-08-20 human downgrade Low -> QA was reasoned explicitly on the BRICK framing ('no permissionless vector; the griefing-brick wording overstated it'). That reasoning does not transfer to the LEAK framing, which is what is live again. Audit recommendation: re-weigh to LOW. Flagged for human decision; the audit does not silently restore a human-set severity.
findings.doNotClose: BINDING, per the entry's own impactInversion_antimatter_02.doNotClose. The disappearance of PhUSDAmountMismatch must never be read as closing this.
findings.law3: Owner footgun, in scope: registering a hook-bearing stablecoin is an ordinary-looking act whose consequence here (mid-call phUSD is swept to a caller-chosen address) is not something a competent non-malicious owner would connect to it. nonReentrant settles RE-ENTRY, not DONATION.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: RECONCILES TO EXISTING LEDGER ENTRY 0ed1c6e3270816c5 (L-03, issueId am1l3, status open, severity low). NO NEW FINGERPRINT. Title and mechanism need rewriting - the entry currently reads 'the stable leg rounds to zero and PhUSDNotReceived kills the whole annihilation', and `PhUSDNotReceived` no longer exists.
findings.verdict: MUST NOT RECONCILE AS `fixed`. The stated BRICK is genuinely gone; what replaced it is worse in kind. The unconditional revert has become a silent settlement in which the caller's entire stablecoin half is taken for zero phUSD. An availability failure was traded for a value failure on the same lines.
findings.description: `PhusdStableMinter.mint` has no non-zero-output guard of its own: it computes `phUSDAmount = (inputAmount * exchangeRate * 10**(18-decimals)) / 1e18` (PhusdStableMinter.sol:242-248) and mints it unconditionally - including when it is 0. At c91bc1a Antimatter refused that case PRE-BURN via `expectedForStable == 0 -> PhUSDNotReceived`. Both the quote and the check are deleted. At 3a96fb7, a zero or near-zero `exchangeRate` produces `mintedForStable == 0`, `totalPhUSD == amount`, and - for any `minPhUSDOut <= amount`, which per CODE-001 is the whole natural-unit range - the call SETTLES. The stablecoin is pulled at :246, deposited to the yield strategy inside `minter.mint` at :251, and :254 confirms it left. The caller gets the antimatter half only.
findings.attackVector: Not an attack - an owner footgun. `PhusdStableMinter` gives its owner three ways to stand a stablecoin down: `pause()` (minter.sol:203 `require(!paused)`), `setStablecoinEnabled(stable,false)` (minter.sol:206 `require(config.enabled)`), and `updateExchangeRate(stable, 0)`. The first two revert INSIDE `minter.mint`, unwinding the whole annihilation safely - test/Annihilation.t.sol:265 test_pausedMinterRollsEverythingBack proves it. The third does NOT revert anywhere. An owner who reaches for `updateExchangeRate(stable, 0)` - or who ratchets a rate down toward zero as ordinary rate management, which the NatSpec at :215-218 explicitly sanctions - gets an outcome categorically different from the other two levers, with no signal that the levers differ. The rounding threshold is low but reachable: for a 6-decimal stable and amount 100e18, `mintedForStable` reaches 0 for any exchangeRate below 1e16.
findings.reachableEndState: A holder annihilating against that pair irreversibly burns their antimatter AND surrenders their full stablecoin half into the yield strategy, receiving phUSD for the antimatter half only - a ~50% loss versus the documented 2x outcome, settling successfully, with `Annihilated` emitted as if normal.
findings.evidenceFromProjectsOwnSuite: test/Annihilation.t.sol:374 test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor executes precisely this: `minter.updateExchangeRate(address(usdc), 0)` followed by a SUCCESSFUL annihilate, asserting `usdc.balanceOf(user) == 0` ('the stable half was still taken'). The suite documents the end state as intended for a zero floor; combined with CODE-001 it is also the end state for every floor a caller is likely to compute.
findings.law3: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun (CLAUDE.md Law 3). This is not 'a malicious owner could' - a malicious owner has better levers. It is that three superficially interchangeable stand-down controls have two safe outcomes and one lossy one, and nothing tells the owner which is which. Test would a competent non-malicious owner be surprised: YES.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Restore a protocol-side floor that does not depend on the caller: `if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` immediately after :256. This costs nothing on the honest path, is independent of `minPhUSDOut`, and re-closes the case the deleted pre-burn check used to close. Note the owner's stated rationale for deleting the pre-burn quote (redundant calculation, fail-fast only worth gas) applies to the PRE-BURN placement, not to a post-mint zero check - a post-mint check needs no `calculateMintAmount` call at all.
findings.severityRecommendation: RE-WEIGH low -> MEDIUM. The entry was Low as a DoS (funds safe, function unavailable). It is now a value failure that settles silently. Flagged for human decision.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: 3aac91383dcb6060 (F-01, issueId am1f1, status FIX-PENDING, low). PROPOSE `fixed`. NOT APPLIED - fix-pending is human-set and this agent has applied nothing.
findings.watchItemAdjudicated: WATCH-02-02 ('F-01 FALSE-CLOSURE WATCH - HIGHEST-PROBABILITY FALSE CLOSURE IN THIS DELTA'). Its closure bar is quoted verbatim: 'evidence of a CALLER-SUPPLIED minimum-output parameter (e.g. `uint256 minPhUSDOut` checked as `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260)'.

barIsMet.callerSuppliedParameterPresent: YES - `uint256 minPhUSDOut`, fourth parameter of annihilate, src/Antimatter.sol:226. It is caller-supplied, in the caller's own transaction, and nothing else can set it.
barIsMet.checkedAgainstAmountPlusMintedForStable: YES - :259 `uint256 totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable;` :260 `if (totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut) revert InsufficientPhUSDOut(minPhUSDOut, totalPhUSD);`. This is the bar's formulation, negated: settle iff amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut.
barIsMet.checkedBeforeSettlement: YES - :260 precedes both payout legs, :263 `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)` and :264 `safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable)`. Nothing settles before the check.
barIsMet.notClosedByCitingTheEqualityCheck: CONFIRMED - the :234/:257 exact-equality pair that WATCH-02-02 forbids citing is DELETED (grep: `PhUSDAmountMismatch` and `calculateMintAmount` have zero occurrences in src/ and test/ at 3a96fb7). It is not being cited; it no longer exists.
barIsMet.boundIsBindingInPractice: test/Annihilation.t.sol:302 test_shortPhUSDMintReverts proves the guard fires on a real rate move: rate halved to 5e17, floor 200 ether, reverts InsufficientPhUSDOut(200e18, 150e18), with the burn rolled back and the stable untouched.

findings.whatTheClosureDOESCover: A caller who states a floor STRICTLY ABOVE `amount` is now genuinely protected against an adverse exchange-rate move between quote and landing, for the whole excess above `amount`, and the failure unwinds the irreversible burn rather than settling short. That is the defect F-01 named - 'no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn' - and it is no longer true.
whatTheClosureDOESNOTCover: The guard is INERT for every minPhUSDOut in [0, amount], including the value a caller most naturally computes. See CODE-001. F-01 closing does not close that; CODE-001 is the residual and must be filed as its own entry.

The guard is ONE-SIDED. It bounds the downside only; the upside bound the deleted PhUSDAmountMismatch used to provide is gone (test/Annihilation.t.sol:335 test_overPhUSDMintNowSucceeds asserts a 150-phUSD stable half is forwarded in full). That un-bounded upside reconciles to existing ledger entry abe4305ac8f0c44f (M-04, wont-fix, 'an unbounded ceiling') - not re-filed here.

The guard is entirely caller-supplied. It replaces a PROTOCOL-side check with an INTEGRATOR obligation. There is no protocol-side floor of any kind on the stablecoin half after this delta. See CODE-003 for the case where that matters.
findings.closureConditions: If a human applies `fixed`, the ledger note must carry the two scope statements above verbatim, so a future reader cannot mistake F-01's closure for coverage of CODE-001 or CODE-003.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: 1b960956475d434a (Q-05, issueId am2q5, status open, qa). PROPOSE `fixed` - MOOT BY DELETION.
findings.description: Q-05 is a defect in text: the comment at c91bc1a:232-233 and the error name `PhUSDAmountMismatch`, which framed an exact-equality quote check as short-change protection. Both artifacts are verified ABSENT at 3a96fb7: `grep -rn 'PhUSDAmountMismatch\|PhUSDNotReceived\|calculateMintAmount' src/ test/` returns zero hits, and the error declarations at the c91bc1a equivalents of :80-83 are replaced by `InsufficientPhUSDOut(uint256 minPhUSDOut, uint256 received)` (src/Antimatter.sol:80-83). The code Q-05 describes does not exist. Closure is by deletion, not by argument.
findings.reweighConditionAdjudicated: Q-05's reweighCondition ('IF F-01 is ever CLOSED, or IF this guard is ever CITED as closing it, re-weigh to LOW') is DISCHARGED, not triggered - exactly as the ledger's fixPlan_2026_08_21 anticipated. F-01 is proposed closed on a genuine caller-supplied parameter (CODE-004), and the equality check is explicitly NOT cited; it is deleted.
findings.residualIsCarriedElsewhereNotHere: The successor NatSpec (:214-225) is honest about the combined-total semantics - it says 'checked against the combined total once both halves are known' and 'in total, counting both halves'. So the misleading-framing defect does not simply relocate. What the new text DOES omit is that [1, amount] is as complete a waiver as 0, while :224-225 presents zero as THE opt-out. That omission is filed under CODE-001.documentationGap, not carried on this fingerprint - Q-05 is about a guard that no longer exists, and reusing it for the new text would blur what was actually fixed.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: GENUINELY NEW as stated. Adjacent to 507e375d3ef4abfe (Q-04, 'Static-analysis findings in audit-harness and mock files') but that entry is a SAST-noise bucket, not a coverage claim - do not collapse into it. Proposed fingerprintBasis `test/Annihilation.t.sol:slippageFloorSuite:GuardRangeUntestable`.
findings.description: No test in the suite can observe the inert range of the new guard, so the suite cannot fail if CODE-001 is ever made worse. The convention stated at :65-67 - 'every test that is not about the slippage floor passes minPhUSDOut == 0' - fixes the non-floor tests at exactly 0, and every dedicated floor test uses a value strictly greater than `amount`: :310 and :352 and :365 use 200 ether against amount 100 ether, :325 uses 150 ether, :341 uses 200 ether. The open interval (0, amount] - 1 wei through 100 ether - is passed by no test at all. Deleting the entire :259-:260 guard would leave the suite green except for the four tests that use a floor above `amount`.
findings.secondDefect: test_zeroExchangeRateReverts (:359) is named for the rate but reverts on the floor. Its expectRevert is `InsufficientPhUSDOut(200 ether, 100 ether)` - the zero exchange rate is not refused by anything; it is the caller's 200-ether floor that refuses it. A reader scanning test names sees 'zero exchange rate reverts' and concludes the protocol rejects a zero rate. It does not; test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor twelve lines later proves the opposite. This name is the exact shape of the false-confidence hazard Q-05 was raised about, relocated from a comment into a test name.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Add a test that passes a floor inside the inert range and asserts what actually happens - e.g. rate 0, amount 100 ether, minPhUSDOut 100 ether, expect SUCCESS with only the antimatter half delivered. Whether that test is later expected to revert (if CODE-001's mitigation lands) or to settle, it is the assertion that pins the boundary. Rename test_zeroExchangeRateReverts to name the floor it is actually testing.
findings.law1Note: Filed because a missing test is what lets a defect regress unseen, and the untested range is precisely the range in which the delta's headline guard does nothing.

reentrancyClassChecklist.note: Walked in full per the mandatory table. Every row is recorded with its basis; no row is silently passed.

rows.basis: The sole local-state write, `_burn(msg.sender, amount)` at :239, precedes every external call. No value-bearing local state is written after any interaction. nonReentrant at :226.

Two guards in series: Antimatter.annihilate is nonReentrant (:226) and PhusdStableMinter.mint is itself nonReentrant (minter.sol:203). Proven by test/Annihilation.t.sol:386 test_reentrantStableIsBlocked, which drives ReentrantStable re-entering annihilate from its transfer hook and asserts ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.

OZ ReentrancyGuard is CONTRACT-WIDE, so annihilate and rescueERC20 share one lock. The unguarded siblings are `mint` (:192, onlyApprovedMinters) and the inherited ERC20 mutators. Re-entering either mid-annihilate reads no stale value: at the moment any external call runs, `_balances[msg.sender]` and `_totalSupply` are already fully settled by :239, and annihilate holds no in-memory balance snapshot of its own state - `stableBefore`/`phUSDBefore` are snapshots of OTHER tokens' balances, which no Antimatter function can move. No shared-state sibling path found.

Enumerated every public/external view: balanceOf/totalSupply/allowance (inherited ERC20), toStableAmount (:283), isApprovedMinter/approvedMinterCount/approvedMinterAt/approvedMinters, phUSD, phUSDMinter, owner. None is a price, share-price, totalAssets or exchange-rate getter, so there is no oracle-shaped surface to consume. toStableAmount is a pure decimals rescale and never reads a rate (profile INV-13). The one transient window that exists is `totalSupply()`: from :239 until :263 the antimatter supply is already burned while the corresponding phUSD has not yet been minted, and untrusted `stable` code runs inside that window at :246 and :251. No in-scope consumer of Antimatter.totalSupply() exists, so this is parked rather than filed.
No ERC721 anywhere in src/ - no _safeMint, no safeTransferFrom, no onERC721Received (profile inboundCallbackHooks, verified).
Same - no ERC1155 surface in src/.

rows.verdict: COVERED BY CODE-002, not separately filed
rows.basis: The value token whose hooks matter is the owner-registered `stable`, whose code runs at :246 and again inside minter.mint at :251. Re-entry is blocked (row 2), but the hook can still make non-reentrant OUTBOUND moves - which is exactly the mid-call phUSD injection vector of CODE-002 / ledger ad4b779566291190. phUSD itself is first-party FlaxToken v2 with no hooks (profile trustAssumption 1).

manualReview.title: Transient totalSupply window during annihilate (read-only-reentrancy shaped, no known consumer)
manualReview.why: From the burn at :239 until the phUSD mint at :263, antimatter totalSupply is reduced but the matching phUSD does not yet exist, and untrusted `stable` code executes inside the window. Any downstream contract that prices off Antimatter.totalSupply() - e.g. a backing-per-token ratio - would read an inconsistent pair. Nothing in scope does this, and Antimatter exposes no price view of its own, so it is not filed. Parked because the exploit would land on an INTEGRATOR, outside this scan's visibility (Law 1).

manualReview.title: The selector change is a safety property and it retires one hypothesis from F-01's fix plan
manualReview.why: F-01's fixPlan_2026_08_21 flagged as a NEW FOOTGUN TO ASSESS 'an integrator whose ABI defaults the new parameter to 0'. ASSESSED, and the concern does not reach: annihilate(address,address,uint256,uint256) is a DIFFERENT SELECTOR from the retired annihilate(address,address,uint256), so an un-migrated integrator hard-reverts on an unknown selector rather than silently sending 0. There is no ABI path that defaults the parameter. The suite even relies on this at :454-458, where the two-argument annihilate(address,uint256) is deliberately listed in the no-burn tripwire as a different-selector control. The live footgun is not a silent default - it is a caller who explicitly passes 0, or (worse, because it looks protective) a value in [1, amount]. Recorded so the fixPlan's line item is answered rather than left hanging.

manualReview.title: Tier-1 detector silence on the delta is a coverage gap, not a clean bill
manualReview.why: Slither, Aderyn, Semgrep and 4naly3er between them produced ZERO records on src/Antimatter.sol:256-266, the lines carrying the whole of story-003's new logic. All three of CODE-001, CODE-002 and CODE-003 live on those lines. Recorded so no downstream stage reads the 0/17-unchanged static delta as evidence that the delta is clean.

manualReview.title: Unbounded upside reconciles to M-04, not re-filed
manualReview.why: Deleting PhUSDAmountMismatch removed the only in-contract bound on how much phUSD the stable half may fetch (test/Annihilation.t.sol:335 asserts a 1.5x rate forwards the whole surplus). This is the ceiling half of existing ledger entry abe4305ac8f0c44f (M-04, wont-fix, 'a hard 1x issuance floor no setting can go below, an unbounded ceiling'). Named here so the loss of the bound is visible in this run's record without minting a duplicate fingerprint against a wont-fix.

manualReview.title: Fee-on-transfer / weird-ERC20 matches - flagged likely-invalid, not dropped
manualReview.why: The :254 post-condition passes for a fee-on-transfer `stable` that moved less than stableAmount and had that lesser quantity consumed (profile settlesWholeOrNotAtAll), and the phUSD transfer at :264 is not re-measured. Both are C4 known-invalid classes (fee-on-transfer not in scope; phUSD is first-party and fee-free). Recorded rather than dropped, per the no-silent-drop rule. Neither is affected by this delta.
